items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One young Egyptian jazz fan that we became well acquainted was called Mimi

ctx.x: Eventually we received news that Willie Lewis had put a complaint against us to the French Labour Government for leaving without giving a notice and we could not come back or would not be permitted to enter France for five years. But that did not worry us because we had a fine jazz orchestra and everything was going swell for us.

One young Egyptian jazz fan that we became well acquainted was called Mimi and his parents owned a very large farm on the outskirts of Alexandria. Mimi's father was a minister in the Egyptian government and was away from the farm quite often, and ever so often Mimi would give a party which would take place in the afternoons. There were two cabarets in Alexandria that engaged European girls as entertainers and Mimi who was a sort of playboy also, would invite some of the girls to those parties and we all had a…

The biggest honour and the most celebrated occasion we experienced was when our orchestra was engaged to play for the wedding reception for the marriage of Mohamed Riza Pahlevi, the crown Prince of Iran (who became later the Shah of Iran) and Princess Fawzia, the sister of King Farouk.
